Explaining Lateness in German: A2 Phrase Practice

Say that you will arrive late, give a brief reason and estimate your arrival in German. Practise Verspätung, sich verspäten and Bescheid geben.

A2 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Useful phrases and patterns

When you expect to be late, state it directly, give a short reason if useful and say when you expect to arrive. Ich verspäte mich uses a reflexive pronoun; Mein Zug hat Verspätung names the delay of the train. Voraussichtlich marks an estimate rather than a guarantee.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not leave out mich in Ich verspäte mich. Distinguish an estimated arrival from a promise by using words such as ungefähr or voraussichtlich.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Ich verspäte mich heute um ungefähr zehn Minuten.I will be about ten minutes late today.
Worked example 2Mein Zug hat Verspätung; ich melde mich, sobald ich mehr weiß.My train is delayed; I will contact you as soon as I know more.
Worked example 3Voraussichtlich bin ich gegen halb drei bei Ihnen.I expect to be with you at around half past two.
Worked example 4Danke fürs Warten, und entschuldigen Sie bitte die Verspätung.Thank you for waiting, and please excuse the delay.

Practice: complete the phrases

Complete the message with the word or verb cue. The situation concerns arrival time, not a project deadline. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Word bank: geben · mich · ungefähr · Verspätung

Question 1. Ich verspäte ___ um einige Minuten. (reflexive, ich)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: mich

Sich verspäten uses mich with ich.

Question 2. Mein Bus hat ___. (delay)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: Verspätung

A vehicle delay is expressed with hat Verspätung.

Question 3. Ich bin ___ in zwanzig Minuten da. (approximately)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: ungefähr

Ungefähr marks the arrival estimate as approximate.

Question 4. Ich wollte Ihnen rechtzeitig Bescheid ___. (give, infinitive)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: geben

The fixed expression is Bescheid geben.

Revise it so it sticks
